rationale: Final iteration. The outer-span lever has now been tested. Iteration 10 (outer sensors at x ±0.040 m, otherwise iteration 6) scored 661.1, below iteration 6's 683.7. Its slalom progress fell from 0.392 to 0.248, so the Evaluator's approval of the ±0.040 candidate, written before it raced, is stale. The Evaluator's decision rule also says to lock iteration 6's settings if the slalom does not move past 0.39, and that condition is met. Earlier single-variable tests all either lowered the slalom or left it flat: base_speed 0.85 (0.364), y 0.075 (0.328), kd 0.6 (0.351). Iteration 6 is the best raced design. It finished 20/20 on the oval (1.99 s) and 20/20 on the s-bend (2.25 s), and the s-bend margin is comfortable. Because this design produces the final unseen-track race and no later iteration can correct it, I lock iteration 6's settings exactly: base_speed 0.9, kp 1.4, ki 0, kd 0.5, sensors at y 0.07 with x ±0.032 m and 16 mm footprints, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], and line_loss last_direction. Body, wheel and mass values are unchanged. Expected result: about 20/20 on the oval and s-bend, and slalom progress near 0.39 with off_track still the likely end. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, so body width cannot help. Hypotheses to check if further data existed: the slalom is limited by its sharpest turns, where max_error reaches the 0.06 m limit, and no tested single lever has moved it past 0.39. Measurements requested per track are the full set, so the held-back-track robustness of this design can be read.
